chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Thal'abah and Abd Allah ibn Hilal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who marows the child of fornication, he said: 'There is no objection; it is disliked merely out of fear of disgrace, and indeed the child belongs to the loins, and indeed the woman is a vessel.' I said: 'A man buys a servant girl who is the child of fornication and has intercourse with her,' he said: 'There is no objection.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying or having intercourse with a child of fornication in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that there is no legal objection to a man marrying or having intercourse with a female slave who is the child of fornication (walad al-zina). The ruling is based on the principle that lineage is determined by the father ('the loins'), and the mother is merely the vessel, so her status as a child of fornication does not impede marriage or consummation. This hadith highlights the Shia juristic distinction between 'walad al-zina' (child of fornication) and 'walad al-shubha' (child of doubt), clarifying that the mother's marital status at conception does not affect the child's lineage or the permissibility of union, provided the 'kharaj' (impurity) is removed.
